classification: single synthetic authenticated browser chat per configuration; no owner preference

method.hardware: same host and synthetic services for paired disposable runs; no inference hardware or real model involved
method.network: internal Docker bridge; UI reached by host browser over bridge IP; Hermes bound to that bridge gateway only
method.identity: fresh synthetic owner account per run
method.measurement: provider captured stream/schema/setup metadata only; Playwright verified visible answer and authenticated chat API persistence
limitations: One run per configuration with instantaneous fake provider; no latency, quality, owner preference, or real-model claim.
The UI task model generated a synthetic title, but the chat retained the derived first-line title; title UX acceptance failed.
Follow-up and tag task completions were requested but no visible output appeared in the captured conversation body.
Open WebUI main answer was visible and persisted in both configurations.
Hermes API session titles are separate metadata and were not shown in the Open WebUI chat list.

The HADES task notification endpoint was deliberately unconfigured in this isolated fixture; its UI poll occurs at page load and every 30 seconds, not per chat message. Production compose requires the feed URL and API key.

interpretation: In this candidate browser flow, default Open WebUI title/follow-up/tag work plus Hermes title upgrades added seven generations to one user answer without a better persisted chat title or visible follow-up/tag output. Disabling the three Open WebUI tasks and Hermes model title upgrade preserved the visible and persisted answer at one generation. This is a strong configuration candidate for usability staging, not a production setting decision: deployed task settings and Hermes title-upgrade state are unknown, and the fake provider cannot qualify task quality. The single task-notification 503 is explained by omitted fixture configuration; production compose requires those settings.
